steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Beat together margarine and sugars until creamy. Add eggs, milk, and vanilla; beat well. Add combined flour, baking soda, and salt; mix well. Stir in oats, chocolate chips, and nuts; mix well.
Drop rounded tablespoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheet. Bake 9 to 10 minutes. Cool for 1 minute on cookie sheet; remove to wire rack.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Chip Oatmeal Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This delicious chocolate chip oatmeal cookie recipe can also be made in bar form. They are simple to make, and the family will love them!
raw_recipe.name: Chocolate Chip Oatmeal Cookies

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Beat together margarine and sugars until creamy. Add eggs, milk, and vanilla; beat well. Add combined flour, baking soda, and salt; mix well. Stir in oats, chocolate chips, and nuts; mix well.
Drop rounded tablespoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheet. Bake 9 to 10 minutes. Cool for 1 minute on cookie sheet; remove to wire rack.

review.reviewBody: They were pretty good! The insides are like cake and the outside is crisp. Don't use this recipe if you are looking for chewy cookies. I recommend adding a little (1/2 tsp. to 1 tsp.) cinnamon also for more flavor. I agree that they were pretty pale -- don't leave them in the oven longer b/c you think they need more color b/c they'll burn! The cinnamon adds a little color also....I bet nutmeg would work well too. I would make them again. They're very fast and relatively easy.

Flavor = b +
Directions/Technique = c-

Flavor to be made 'perfect' (in my palette's opinion):
2 teaspoon vanilla
1/2 teaspoon nutmeg
1/2 cup more oats
1 teaspoon cinnamon
No nuts for me:)

Technique changes:
1) sift dry ingredients together--no flat cookies that way
2) I made the cookies and the bar version (in a 8x8 glass), the bar version turned out amazing and will be my 'go to version' now

I thought these were lovely cookies! I halved the recipe and forgot to add the milk; but they turned out great! I would consider maybe using a bit less sugar and/or adding a bit more salt next time (and leave out the milk on purpose since they came out so well!). I liked them better when I flattened them slightly before baking--they came out a bit nicer shaped, and were chewier that way. They also needed 12-14 minutes to bake for me. Half the recipe gave me about 24 1.5-tbsp sized balls of dough. Thank you for sharing your recipe!

I followed the recipe, except only used 1/2 c of walnuts and baked as bar cookies. I did butter the 13x9 pan as I was worried they would stick. Cooked about 35 mins and they came out wonderfully. This is definitely a keeper!!

I found this recipe a couple years ago and have been using it ever since. Everyone who tries my cookies loves them (even if they don't usually like oatmeal chocolate chip cookies). After experimenting with this recipe, a few things I do differently are: melt the butter (but not completely), use about 3/4 of the salt that it calls for, don't use the walnuts, make the cookies a little bigger (and cook them for 12 minutes), and let them sit on the hot cookie sheet for 4 minutes before letting them cool.

Yum! I made a few substitutions and additions. 1 jar zucchini apple cinnamon baby food (large jar presidents choice organic) and 4 heaping tbsp organic applesauce (these two pureed measured 1cup) in place of butter. i also coarsely chopped a can of chickpeas and added in at the end with the chocolate chips and chopped nuts (I pulsed the nuts and chickpeas together in my food processor until they were a crumbly texture. I also added 1tsp cinnamon and 1 tsp vanilla. I had no brown sugar so I used 3/4 cup sugar cane sugar in place of both the white and brown sugar-they turned out plenty sweet enough. I also added 3tbsp of milled flax at the end. Because of the addition of chickpeas there was enough to make two trays. I only had to cook them for 25min. My kids (and my husband) loved them!! This is a healthy and protein packed version! They are however a bit cakey from the addition of a fruit and veg puree. Enjoy

Tried this recipe and I really liked it! I did change a few things because when I made recipe as is, the cookies came out flat and a bit too salty. The second time I added more flour- 2 and a half cups- and less salt. I also put the recipe in the fridge for awhile before cooking. Then my cookies came out amazing! My brother ate them all in two days!

We thought they are great! I did sub 3/4c of whole wheat flour and used unbleached all purpose flour (pretending this makes them healthy lol) for the other cup and dark chocolate, not semi-aweet. I used a large cookie dough scoop for some of them and smaller scoop for others. Larger ones took 11m to cook, smaller I cooked 8-9 depending on how they looked after 8. Will post pic to show difference. Mine were a bit crispy on the outside and cheewy on the inside right after they cooled enough to eat! Have not had one since they completely cooled but think they will be just as good. Also, will make again as this kind of cookie (chocolate oatmeal) is one of our favs. Thanks for recipe
I followed the recipe pretty much with the exception of using half Crisco and half butter. I also added a half a teaspoon of baking powder. AMAZING cookies. I baked at 350 for 12 minutes. YUMMY!
I added an extra tsp. of vanilla, used hershey's special dark chocolate chips, left out the walnuts, and baked for 8 min. @ 350 degrees - they are fantastic!!

Followed recipe but for omitting milk (saw no need), adding 1/2 tsp baking powder & substituting pecans for walnuts - cookies were perfect. Baking time & temp was spot on. Love the amount of nuts & chocolate chips called for. Will definitely make again.
This is honestly my favorite oatmeal cookie recipe. I use dark chocolate chips and they rarely last past the second day. The only tweak I make is just adding a bit of cinnamon.
First time making these so I only did smallest batch, first pan came out runny so I read some of the tip, an added more flower( 1/4 cup) . There perfect now. Smile 😊 Thanks yall for the tips.
Yummy! Definitely a five star cookie.
nasty just nasty promise me it was not good at all, I couldn’t eat it, it just looked disgusting. I don’t recommend this please😭🙏
Great recipe! Used cranberries instead of chocolate chips and chopped almonds on top. Yum
